question: Does sustained original W-loop host-memory growth arise during backward, optimizer or diagnostics, and depend on constant/scheduledLR or full/reduced sampled observations?

design.question: Does sustained original W-loop host-memory growth arise during backward, optimizer or diagnostics, and depend on constant/scheduledLR or full/reduced sampled observations?
design.data: Same original first512 ordered realTRAIN occurrences per fresh B0 condition; no DEV/TEST read.
design.hardware: Sequential logical32–63/physical8–15, each at most2400s, OMP/MKL2 as original. Wait for complete backward-only batch closure first.
design.precision: Unchanged BF16 parameters/gradients and FP32 master/Adam; same native full-head gate, initial exact masters, one ZeRO reducer, finite gradients/norm each update.
design.reduced: Skip sampled master/model/replica observations after first3 through15; perform them again at16. Omitted values are null. First3/full state finite scans preserved.
design.measurement: Per-rank RSS/glibc counters before backward, after backward, after optimizer, after sampled diagnostics and complete update. External process-tree PSS/availableRAM every10s. XLA metrics1/3/8/16. Individual process PSS is primary; do not treat summed RSS as private memory.
design.endpoint: Tail9–16 complete-update PSS/RSS slope and stage deltas, complete-step and component/optimizer times, module/compilation/cache changes. Candidate bounded tail<=64MiB/rank/update;16 updates cannot establish long-run steady state.
design.stop: External512GiB available floor, finite timeouts, exact-owned TERM then35s surviving-group KILL, no retries, no scientific use of these models.
limits: No causal attribution from a single graph/cache log; this is an explicit2x2 probe.
Sequential order may affect cold caches; cold/setup costs separate from tail timings.
Per-step memory instrumentation itself is extra, shared across all conditions.
No checkpoints emitted: short disposable engineering profiles do not qualify long training or resumption.

scheduled_full.tail: updates9-16; all scheduled updates remain inside20-update warmup
scheduled_full.glibc_live_definition: mallinfo2.uordblks + mallinfo2.hblkhd; allocator accounting, not a C++ root-cause attribution

conclusion: All four conditions retain substantial private host memory. Constant LR and reduced sampled diagnostics do not remove the live-allocation growth. Flat live tensor counts coexist with repeatedly created compile handles; cache-capacity is the next causal test, not an established cause.
limits: All16 scheduled updates in v1 are inside the original20-update warmup. This batch cannot assess later cosine transitions or the original step64 model export.
Saved-model evaluation and CPU checks overlapped conditions. Step times are descriptive under that load, not a clean causal speed comparison.
No checkpoints were emitted; this is not a recovery or long-memory qualification.
mallinfo2 growth can include retained runtime/cache allocations; these counters cannot identify ownership.
One rapidly growing rank per adjacent pair is an observation, not proof of collective/runtime causation.
Sequential order/cold cache differences and overlapping work prevent causal timing comparisons.
The smaller static-weight world1 backward-only probe did not reproduce this full-loop growth.
